content.value_statement: React apps often slow down because data, bundles, rendering, and state updates interact in complex ways. This skill applies Vercel performance guidance to help agents write, review, and refactor React and Next.js code.
actual_capabilities: Guides agents through React and Next.js performance review patterns.
Identifies async waterfalls and suggests safer parallel data fetching patterns.
Recommends bundle-size improvements using direct imports and dynamic loading.
Explains server caching with React cache, LRU caches, and serialization boundaries.
Covers client fetching, re-render control, rendering work, and JavaScript hot paths.
limitations: It is a guidance skill, not an automated profiler or benchmark runner.
It does not replace framework documentation for version-specific API behavior.
It cannot prove performance gains without measuring the target application.
Some recommendations require project context before they are safe to apply.

use_cases.title: Review a Pull Request
use_cases.description: Find React and Next.js performance issues before code merges into production.

use_cases.title: Refactor Slow Pages
use_cases.description: Prioritize fixes for waterfalls, heavy bundles, redundant fetching, and excess re-renders.

use_cases.title: Guide Code Generation
use_cases.description: Generate new components that follow Vercel performance patterns from the start.

prompt_templates.title: Check Basic Component Performance
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review of a single React component.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this React component for avoidable re-renders, unnecessary effects, and simple rendering issues. Explain the top fixes first.

prompt_templates.title: Improve Next.js Data Fetching
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate review of page or route data flow.
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze this Next.js page for async waterfalls and redundant requests. Suggest changes using early promises, parallel fetching, and cache boundaries.

prompt_templates.title: Reduce Bundle Size
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced bundle review for a feature area.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review these imports and component boundaries for bundle cost. Recommend direct imports, dynamic imports, and user-intent preloading where appropriate.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Full Performance Refactor
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a prioritized React and Next.js performance refactor plan for this feature. Cover data fetching, bundle size, caching, rendering, and validation steps.

output_examples.input: Review a dashboard page that loads user data, charts, and a large editor.
output_examples.output: A prioritized review that flags data waterfalls, recommends lazy editor loading, and separates critical content from deferred widgets.

output_examples.input: Improve a component that re-renders many rows after every state update.
output_examples.output: A refactor plan that narrows dependencies, extracts memoized children, and moves expensive calculations closer to their usage.

output_examples.input: Assess a Next.js route that repeats authentication and database lookups.
output_examples.output: A caching recommendation that separates per-request deduplication from cross-request caching and explains measurement points.

best_practices: Measure the current bottleneck before applying broad performance changes.
Apply high-impact rules first, especially waterfalls and bundle-size fixes.
Keep correctness, accessibility, and security checks in every performance refactor.
anti_patterns: Do not add memoization everywhere without evidence of repeated expensive work.
Do not defer critical above-the-fold content just to improve initial bundle size.
Do not copy inline script patterns without validating data sources and CSP requirements.

faq.question: What does this skill help with?
faq.answer: It helps AI agents apply React and Next.js performance guidance during coding, review, and refactoring tasks.

faq.question: Does it run benchmarks automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance and review criteria. You still need profiling or production metrics to confirm improvements.

faq.question: Is this only for Next.js projects?
faq.answer: No. Many rules apply to React apps generally, while some server and routing guidance is specific to Next.js.

faq.question: Can it rewrite code directly?
faq.answer: The skill guides an agent that can edit code. The final changes depend on the agent and project permissions.

faq.question: Which tools can use it?
faq.answer: The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: How should teams adopt it?
faq.answer: Start with pull request reviews, then use it for targeted refactors where profiling shows clear performance problems.
